identification: Plain two-tone stoneware demijohn/flagon, tan (Bristol/Albany-style) glazed shoulder and neck over cream salt-glazed body, strap handle, about 30 cm, probably early 20th century Australian or English. No maker's stamp visible on body or base.
marks_seen: Photo 1 shows side view with lot tag; no stamp or transfer print on the body. Photo 2 shows the base: plain unglazed, dirty, no mark, impressed number or maker stamp visible.
google_searches: antique stoneware demijohn two tone salt glaze unmarked 30cm value. Carter's guide: advertising and unmarked stoneware demijohns late 19th C, 10 auction results $40 to $2012, median $222 (the high end is advertising pieces, not plain ones). Gumtree plain demijohn jugs about $45 each; Etsy two-tone jug $60-80.

entries.note: Large vintage/antique stoneware salt glazed flagon, early 1900s, auction, 3 bids. Excludes postage.

viewing_check: Estimate $20-30, current bid $20 (+22% premium). Check for cracks, chips, crazing and a stamp on the shoulder or base that the photos did not show. Unmarked plain examples sell about $27-35 on eBay; only marked Australian potters or advertising pieces reach $100+. Prices mostly within 3 years, flat.
searches_tried: Google unmarked two-tone demijohn value; Terapeak AU 'stoneware demijohn' (50 rows, mostly marked pieces); Terapeak AU 'stoneware flagon jug' (9 rows).
flip_reason: Plain unmarked, bulky and fragile to post. About 2 comparable unmarked sales at $27-35 vs current bid $20 plus premium.

identification: Single copper timpani (kettle drum) bowl, no head, with 8 hand-screw tuning rods with chrome T-handles on brass brackets, small brass carry handle, three small feet. About 50 cm high x 60 cm dia per the description. Looks like an old (probably 1920s-50s) hand-tuned student or band timpani shell, not a modern pedal timpani. No maker's plate, stamp or label seen.
marks_seen: Photo 1: front with lot tag, 8 chrome T-handle rods, copper patina and verdigris inside. Photo 2: close of rods and brass bracket, no stamp. Photo 3: underside, hammered/dented bowl, three feet, no maker mark or plate visible. No head, no stand.
google_searches: copper timpani kettle drum bowl hand tuned T-handle antique orchestral timpani value. Results: eBay US pre-owned timpani from US$400; 1stDibs copper timpani used as a centre table; Drum Forum 2016 old-school tympani about US$250-350 each; Reverb vintage Ludwig 27-1/4 in copper kettle drum US$199 local pickup; new AU copper timpani A$5,000 to $12,000.

entries.note: Vintage Ludwig copper kettle timpani drums WITH original stand, fixed price, free postage listed; likely a set with heads and stand, so not like for like with a single bare shell. Converted by Terapeak to AU$.
Vintage copper kettle drum 27-1/4 in, local pickup only, asking. No rate used.
Poster paid about $250 for a set of old-school timpani; old and unsuitable for modern music.

viewing_check: Estimate $80-160, current bid $40 (+22% premium). Bulky and awkward to post. Only one vaguely comparable sale found (a Ludwig pair with stand). Check bowl for splits or dents, whether the rods all work, and for a maker's plate. Value is mainly decorative or as a planter or table base.
searches_tried: Google vintage copper timpani value; Terapeak AU 'copper timpani' (1 row, miniature); Terapeak US 'vintage copper timpani kettle drum' (2 rows); Terapeak AU 'kettle drum copper' (1 irrelevant row).
flip_reason: Bulky shell, 0 close comparable sales; only a Ludwig set with stand at A$582 in Jul 2025. Current bid $40.

marks_seen: No maker name, stamp or label on base, peg or rings. Rope appears hemp/sisal with wire-less twisted construction, base worn with black painted edge.

identification: M. Hohner diatonic 10-button melodeon/accordion, Made in Germany, with red end labels reading 'Highest Award San Francisco 1915' and 'Steel Bronze Reeds' (Hohner's Panama-Pacific Exposition award issue, produced for years after 1915, so the 1915 is a medal date not a build date). Wooden ends with pressed metal corner plates, green and red paper bellows with a visible hole/tear in one fold, leather hand strap. Condition poor, sold AS IS.
marks_seen: Left end label: 'Highest Award SAN FRANCISCO 1915', 'STEEL BRONZE REEDS'. Right end label: 'M. HOHNER ACCORDION Made in Germany'. Bellows has a hole on the left side near the first folds. Only one photo exists for the lot.
google_searches: M. Hohner accordion 'Highest Award San Francisco 1915' steel bronze reeds. Found eBay and Reverb listings of the same model (Reverb asking US$90 used; eBay asking US$180 'Vintage M Hohner Diatonic Button Accordion Melodeon'), JustAnswer note that it is a German M. Hohner San Francisco 1915 award button accordion, Invaluable 'Antique Hohner Best Made Accordion' lot (steel reeds, San Francisco 1915, shows wear).

viewing_check: Estimate $20-30, current bid $10 (+22% premium). Only one photo. The bellows has a visible hole, so check bellows, reeds sounding, wooden ends for cracks and missing buttons. Exact-match sales on eBay over 3 years run $36-175 (AU$), median about $80; working or clean ones $110-175, as-is and rough ones $36-55. Prices stable, no clear trend.
searches_tried: Google Hohner 1915 San Francisco; Terapeak AU 'hohner accordion 1915' (0 rows); AU 'hohner accordion vintage' (50 rows, mostly larger piano or bigger button models); AU 'm hohner antique accordion' (0 rows); US 'hohner accordion 1915 san francisco' (8 rows, all same model); US 'hohner accordion steel bronze reeds' (18 rows).
flip_reason: 8 exact-match sales (US-listed, AU$ shown) typical $55-110 (median about $80, best $175). Current bid $10 so cost about $12 with premium. Small and posts cheaply. A $100 profit needs a working example at the $110+ end; with a holed bellows 'as is' this is a likely $40-60 outcome, so only a possible flip.

identification: Set of five red enamel kitchen canisters with black script lettering (Sugar, Rice, Tea, Coffee, Flour), black rims and black knobs, plus a small red enamel pouring saucepan/milk pan with black handle (6 pieces). Rice and Flour canisters have no lids; Tea lid has a worn/repaired knob area; wear and chips likely (sold AS IS). Probably 1930s-50s, maker unknown (candidates: Australian or European enamelware; Nylex, Gayware and Norton sets are similar).
marks_seen: Lettering Sugar, Rice, Tea, Coffee, Flour in black script on red. Lot tag 108 on Sugar lid and a small old inventory sticker on the Flour canister. No maker's mark readable (only one photo, no base shots).
google_searches: vintage red enamel canister set sugar rice tea coffee flour black lettering Australian value. Found Instagram vintage dealer set of 5 1930s cream and red enamel with Bakelite knobs $225 asking; Facebook Nylex 1950s set of five (sold); Gumtree vintage canister sets $90-150 asking; Etsy sets AU$112-179 asking.

flip_reason: About 9 relevant sales, typical $50-100 for sets (complete good ones to $182), but this set lacks two lids and is bulky to post; margin on a likely $40-60 winning bid plus premium is under $100.
